body:
Review pass 6. ESCALATION plus a verified proposal.

Epic 2 moved to doing with bd-01KZXBD69V5PFTKTVBXDNKZT7J (p0) still open. That bead decides what the coherent covector a IS and how frame weights compose with a general metric - and Epic 2 acceptance already writes a = w/sum(w), which presumes an answer recorded nowhere. R/metric.R does not exist yet, so this is the cheapest moment. Rather than just re-flagging, I derived and numerically verified a resolution; accept, reject or amend, but please record it before the file lands.

PROPOSAL: the frame supplies support and a diagonal reweighting, the metric supplies the inner product, composing as

  K_eff,x = D(w_x)^(1/2) K_x D(w_x)^(1/2)

Verified (k=7, q=4, cross-partition):
- reduces EXACTLY to the current diagonal frame at K = I: max|K_eff - D(w)| = 2.2e-16, so no existing result changes
- preserves PSD for a precision metric (min eig 0.045) and preserves your exact component split: min eig K_coh = -2.3e-18, min eig K_cfg = 3.7e-17, max|K_coh + K_cfg - K_eff| = 6.9e-18
- coherent amplitude stays the raw weighted regional mean, 2.8e-17
- closed form: a^T K_eff^-1 a = (1/W^2) sqrt(w)^T Sigma sqrt(w), collapsing to 1/W at Sigma = I, which matches the value I verified against your current implementation in pass 1

BONUS - this resolves bd-01KZXBDP92BNX44VWW08M35VQZ at zero cost. That closed form needs Sigma, the shrunk residual covariance the learner already holds BEFORE inversion. No solve, no factorization. The O(k^3) per support per edge concern disappears, provided the handle exposes the covariance or a quadform entry point rather than only apply_K.

CONSERVATION - settled by the same experiment. With conservative normalization:
  Sigma = I            : max|sum_x K_eff,x - I| = 2.2e-16  -> conservation HOLDS
  local precisions     : differs from any global metric by O(1) (0.964) -> conservation LOST
So it is a feature-additive-only capability, and the README claim needs the same gate Epic 8 already applies to the searchlight-cost claim.

I do not recommend the other two candidates: replacing weights entirely discards the scale convention that makes searchlight sizes comparable, and refusing the combination rejects something that is well defined and reduces correctly.

Also noted: your recorded decision on bd-01KZXD7G0E5KEDMC2VCGVKGNS7 - canonical accumulation order, block size not part of scientific identity unless canonical execution proves infeasible - is the right call and matches what the existing .canonical_reduce machinery already guarantees elsewhere.
